notes.mathematical-ai-safety-institute: maisi.org confirms that it is an independent nonprofit. It also confirms Tsimerman (Scientific Director, 2026 Fields Medallist), Critch (Executive Director), Jake Ross (COO), $10M from Coefficient Giving as of 16 Sep 2026, 10-30 faculty for January 2027, 30-100 for the September 2027 Special Year, and that members must move to the Bay Area. Press coverage (cryptobriefing, dnyuz/NYT syndication, theoutpost) confirms the 8 Sep 2026 launch, Tsimerman joining OpenAI's safety team while MAISI runs independently, and Critch as co-founder. Its scientific advisory panel (Gowers, Vakil, Irving, Christiano) could be mentioned. The one change is to the superlative 'largest funded channel yet', which nothing I found supports, so I softened it; I also added the founder roles. Ring, tags and status are fine.
notes.xor-labs: xorlabs.org confirms: director Fernando Rosas; members Kolchinsky, Jansma and Ehrlich, plus Gutknecht, Boyd and Vardakostas; based in London; funders UK AISI, Coefficient Giving and AISTOF; the three research lines; the publications cited with their venues and years (Nature Rev Phys 2026, PNAS 2025, RLJ 2025, NeurIPS 2026); the exact 'macro-agent'/'micro-agents' wording; Laukkonen and Kringelbach in its collaborators list; and the Sussex contact address. Iliad's incubated-organizations page lists XOR Labs. One small point: the site calls itself 'a research organisation' and never states that it is a nonprofit, so org_type nonprofit is an inference (it could go in caveats). Tags are valid and sensible.
notes.stormglass-ai-safety-institute: stormglass.ca matches the mission quote, the 'under construction' note and the absence of named staff. PrincInt's affiliates page confirms Max Hennick as leader and the former name MoirAI. Iliad lists Stormglass (Canada). The researcher page gives Fredericton, NB, $120-160k, and 'not currently hiring' until more funding comes. The research-engineer page, however, says that as of 28 June 2026 they had 'found a suitable candidate', so the role was filled rather than paused; I corrected that. The paper is right: 'Almost Bayesian: Dynamics of SGD Through Singular Learning Theory' is at ICLR 2026 (proceedings.iclr.cc); the arXiv v1 had a different title. One taxonomy point: the status guide says a name change counts as 'changed', but unverified is defensible given how thin the site is.
notes.alignment-journal: The LessWrong 'Coming Soon' post is dated 3 Mar 2026 (authors include MacKinlay, Riedel, Murfet, Aaronson, Kulveit, Hutter). The blog lists posts on 6 Apr (Features and policies), 28 Apr and 1 Sep 2026 (Organization, Personnel, and Scope). The 1 Sep post confirms the managing editors Riedel and MacKinlay, head of operations Kristi Uustalu, and a senior editorial board that includes Lazar, Saxe and Murfet. The current site shows three papers under review with 'nominate yourself to review' links and nothing published yet, which matches the caveats. Iliad lists it, launching fall 2026. Tags are valid, and the media role/org_type is defensible.

notes.astera-institute: astera.org/team confirms the titles: McCaleb Co-Founder & CEO (Neuro & AGI), Tsao Chief Scientist (Neuro), George Head of AI Research. Seemay Chou is the other co-founder (President, Foundation). Founding in 2020 by McCaleb and Chou matches Forbes coverage. The $1B+ for AGI, $600M for neuroscience and Dileep George's Feb 2026 arrival from DeepMind are all confirmed (astera.org/?p=1624, Forbes AU). Byrnes is a Research Fellow at Astera. I changed the ring from core to bridge. Under rule E, Astera's primary mission is not making AI go well: it is a 2020 philanthropic science institute that also has life-sciences (Radial), open-science and residency divisions. Its main AI effort is building brain-inspired AGI, which aisafety.com files under 'Capabilities research'. Its explicitly safety work is Byrnes, plus Simplex, which is profiled separately. That fits 'rooted elsewhere with an AI-safety programme' (bridge), not an AI-safety org. Everything else checks out. Minor point: I could not confirm on the current site that the 'Obelisk' name is still in use for the AGI programme, so consider saying 'its AGI programme'.

notes.ai-safety-behavioural-modelling-group-te: FLI 2018 grant 'Incentives for Safety Agreement Compliance in AI Race', $224,747, PI The Anh Han at Teesside: confirmed. The Teesside profile confirms him as Professor of Computer Science leading the Centre for Digital Innovation, the EPSRC 'Evolutionary Game Theory Under Uncertainty' grant (2024-27), FLI projects on AI governance and safe development behaviours, and that he takes PhD students in AI safety. arXiv 2603.24742: v1 (25 Mar 2026) was titled 'Trust as Monitoring: Evolutionary Dynamics of User Trust and AI Developer Behaviour', but the v2 revision (3 Aug 2026) is now 'Trust or Check? Understanding the (Evolutionary) Dynamics of User Trust in AI Systems', so I updated the title. It is a 24-author collaboration led by Adeela Bashir and Han, which supports the caveat about heavy co-authorship. I did not check the FAIRGAME and Journal of Theoretical Biology items. Ring bridge and tags are fine. Sources: research.tees.ac.uk/en/persons/the-anh-han, futureoflife.org/2018-ai-grant-recipients, arxiv.org/abs/2603.24742 (v1 and v2).

Together with the four-part Mentoring the Machines (2023–Apr 2024), which frames AI alignment as cultivating wisdom, this is a sustained publication line in 2024–26 with an explicit alignment/'going well' framing. That meets bridge, not potential. Adjacent doesn't fit, because adjacent excludes alignment framing. I dropped engagement 'partner', which applies only to entries with no AI programme. I confirmed vervaekefoundation.org 301-redirects to johnvervaeke.com. Flag for the orchestrator: this is individual-led and the context excludes individuals, so consider listing Vervaeke as a notable individual instead. Sources: sites.libsyn.com/480795/2025/05, johnvervaeke.com, abebooks listing (Story Grid Publishing 2023).
notes.flourishing-intelligence-program-centre-: theflip.ai confirms the host (Centre for Eudaimonia and Human Flourishing, Linacre College), Laukkonen as Programme Director and Kringelbach as Centre Director, Cillo family funding, and partners Deco (UPF) and Vuust (Aarhus). The team page confirms Chandaria (Senior Advisor and founding member) and Surya Cillo (Senior Advisor and donor). A UPF news item confirms the joint launch. arXiv 2605.10310 'Positive Alignment' was submitted 11 May 2026, led by Laukkonen with Kringelbach. arXiv 2609.35618 was submitted 28 Sep 2026; Laukkonen and Kringelbach are co-authors. It is led by Shamil Chandaria (FLIP senior advisor) with Seth, Shanahan, Legg and others, so 'co-authored' is accurate but they are not lead authors. I did not verify the Dec 2025 launch month or the July 2026 'Clear Mind' paper. Ring bridge, status new and tags are valid.
notes.monash-centre-for-consciousness-and-cont: arXiv 2504.15125 confirms the eight authors (Laukkonen first), April 2025, and the AILuminate and Prisoner's Dilemma prompt results. Monash pages and search snippets say M3CS was 'established in 2021' with A$12M from the Hoskings' Three Springs Foundation; the 'opens' article dates to March 2021 (cited by gawlerblog 9 Mar 2021). I found no support for an opening in 2022, so I removed it. The summary now names Laukkonen as lead author so the paper doesn't read as the centre's own work. The URL is the official one (it appears in search indexes) but returns 403 to bots; monash.edu/research/M3CS is an alternative. Ring, tags and status look fine. Sources: arxiv.org/abs/2504.15125, monash.edu/news/articles/world-first-centre-for-consciousness-and-contemplative-studies-opens-at-monash-university, lens.monash.edu (19 Apr 2021).
notes.re-align: The 2026 site confirms the 27 Apr 2026 date at ICLR, the eight organisers and their affiliations (EPFL, MIT/UCSF, MPI Psycholinguistics, NYU/UAlberta, Berkeley, Stanford, NYU/Purdue, UW-Madison/Amazon), the neural-control theme tied to 'safer, steerable models', the travel grants and the challenge leaderboard. I couldn't verify the submission-growth figures (303 to 688). The safety framing is thin, as the caveats say; bridge is borderline but defensible. Source: representational-alignment.github.io/2026.
notes.bramley-computational-cognitive-science-: The lab's publication page confirms 'The cognitive science of AI alignment' (Voudouris, Roberts-Gaal, Bramley, Sucholutsky, Summerfield) as a workshop paper in the Proceedings of the 48th CogSci (2026), quoting UK AISI's 'alarmingly'. The site resolves (200). Lowering the ring to potential for a single co-organised workshop is reasonable. Source: bramleylab.ppls.ed.ac.uk/publication/2026-01-01_voudouris2026alignment/.
notes.nyu-center-for-mind-ethics-and-policy: The about page gives 2022 launch, permanent centre in 2024 with a $6M endowment, Sebo as director (Associate Professor of Environmental Studies), and Lederman, Sims and Fogel in the roles listed. It states the mission as 'special focus on animals and AI', not 'invertebrates and AI'; invertebrates was the early programme's framing, so I corrected it. The events page confirms the 2 Sep 2026 J-Space event, the 2 Jul 2026 event, and the 10-11 Apr 2026 summit and 12 Apr workshop. The events page doesn't show the 2027 summit date (9-10 Apr 2027), so it is unverified. The Long, Sebo and Sims paper is in Philosophical Studies 182(7), 2025. Ring and tags are fine. Sources: nonhumanminds.org/about, nonhumanminds.org/events, link.springer.com/10.1007/s11098-025-02343-7.
notes.cambridge-digital-minds: The site confirms Caviola as director, the home in the Leverhulme CFI (Institute for Technology and Humanity), and Shevlin, Saad and Ladak in the roles stated. The fellowship page confirms 3-9 Aug 2026 at Jesus College, 15 fellows, a £1,000 stipend, and partners Rethink Priorities and PRISM, with no funder named. I couldn't confirm the '3,600 applicants' and '3,000 course applicants' figures on the pages I fetched. Core vs bridge is a judgement call; core is defensible given its founding AI-welfare mission and ties to the EA and AI-safety ecosystem. Sources: digitalminds.cam, digitalminds.cam/fellowship.
notes.sussex-centre-for-consciousness-science: The people page confirms Seth as director and Barrett, Bosten and Sawyer as deputy directors. James Stone (BSMS) is a fourth deputy, an omission but not an error. Founding in 2010 as the Sackler Centre is correct. Seth's 'The Mythology of Conscious AI' won the 2025 Berggruen Prize Essay Competition and is published in Noema. The TED talk 'Why AI is unlikely to become conscious' was given on the main stage in Vancouver in April 2026. All key_work items check out. Sources: sussex.ac.uk/.../people, sussex.ac.uk/broadcast/read/69852, sussex.ac.uk/broadcast/read/70671, ted.com/talks/anil_seth_why_ai_is_unlikely_to_become_conscious.
notes.center-for-the-future-of-ai-mind-society: The live site uses the name 'Center for the Future of AI, Mind & Society (AIMS)' and confirms Schneider, Bailey (Associate Director) and Barenholtz (Assistant Director). The members page lists Kilian as 'Artificial Intelligence and Global Catastrophic Risk Fellow', with roughly 7 core team, 29 faculty, 15 fellows and 15 students. That is about 50 staff, faculty and fellows, not 'about 70 affiliated faculty and fellows', so I corrected the count. FAU news confirms MindFest 2023 marked the centre's grand opening, so founded 2023 is acceptable with the caveat. The NSF Smart Streetscapes caveat is correct. The catastrophic framing is shaky, given Schneider's deflationary 2026 line on chatbots; structural or critical might fit as well, but I left it. Sources: fau.edu/future-mind/, fau.edu/future-mind/members/, fau.edu/artsandletters/news/mindfest-2023-post/.
notes.the-human-line-project: Checked the official site and its /research page. 'Delusions and Harms Associated with AI Chatbot Use' with King's College London is dated 07/09/2026 and covers 185 reports. 'AI-Induced Delusional Spirals' with Stanford is dated 13/04/2026. The site shows recent activity (a podcast on 28 Sep 2026). The tags are valid keys, and the bridge/adjacent borderline is already stated in the caveats. Character.AI (filed autumn 2024), Carrier v. OpenAI Foundation (Jun 2026), Lines v. OpenAI Foundation (Jul 2026) and Winters v. OpenAI (Jul 2026). 'Designing Technology Remedies' is dated May 2026. notes.human-centered-ai-lab-university-of-oxfo: hailab.ox.ac.uk confirms it was founded in 2024 by Philipp Koralus, McCord Professor of Philosophy and AI and Founding Director. It sits in the Faculty of Philosophy and is linked to the Institute for Ethics in AI. Lehman and Danenberg are listed as Senior Research Associates, and Mat Dryhurst is also listed. The four projects (PyETR, Inquiry Complex, Humans In Humans Out, Blueprint) are on the site, as is the 2026 Cosmos HAI Lab Lecture by Jack Clark. I did not check the Venice panel. The bridge ring is defensible but generous, since its framing is human flourishing rather than safety.
notes.cosmos-institute: Zoe Weinberg is not on the team page (cosmos-institute.org/team), and a search found no link between her and Cosmos grants, so I removed her. The Institute for Decentralized AI was launched by incubation fellow Samuele Marro (blog post dated 1 Oct 2025), not by Cosmos itself, so I reworded that. I could not verify the 23,000 Substack subscribers or the roughly $75k fellowship figure, so I dropped them from the summary. Everything else checks out: HQ in Austin per the homepage, which also lists a London team presence (so the london hub tag is OK), grant sizes and the $1M FIRE pool, and the round that closed 26 July 2026 (grants page). The blog archive shows 80 grantees announced 2 Sep 2026, Cosmos Ventures in 'Dare To Found' on 16 Sep 2026, and an essay on 2 Oct 2026. Founding in 2024 matches TechCrunch and SiliconANGLE (Sept 2024 launch).
notes.uk-ai-security-institute: aisi.gov.uk/about confirms Hogarth as Chair, de Zoete as Director, Leung as CTO and Summerfield as Research Director, along with £66m a year, 100+ technical staff and its place under DSIT. The research page lists 'Ask don't tell' (Human Influence, 28 Apr 2026), 'The levers of political persuasion' (18 Jul 2025) and RealityTest (8 Jun 2026), and has a Societal Resilience area. The Alignment Project site shows £27m+ to 60+ projects, the co-funders as listed, and that a similar 2026 round is unlikely. Core ring and public org type follow the taxonomy's own examples.
notes.friends-of-attention: 'Attensity!' came out in January 2026 from Crown, a PRH imprint (Penguin in the UK), edited by Burnett, Loh and Schmidt (Porchlight, Penguin UK, Linden Tree listings), not in 2025. Search results name Burnett as director of SoRA and Schmidt as its Program Director, so the caveat that Burnett's role rests only on memory is out of date. The origins (2018 São Paulo Biennial, 2019 gathering) and the Institute for Sustained Attention as a 501(c)(3) are confirmed on friendsofattention.org/about. Burnett's AI talks are light, personal engagement, so potential and none_yet are still defensible, but 'no AI work found' overstates it.
notes.mit-initiative-on-technology-and-self: Turkle's bios (e.g. Hedgehog Review, WGBH, web.mit.edu/people/sturkle) give her as founder (2001) and director of the initiative, so I filled the founding year and removed the caveat that it is unknown. sherryturkle.mit.edu confirms that 'Artificial Intimacy' was published by Little, Brown in September 2026. The adjacent ring, psych_relational (the taxonomy's own example) and the other tags are fine.
notes.compassion-aligned-machine-learning: Checked: the team page (Tidmarsh, Brazilek, Chaudhary and adviser Sebo are correct; registered in California); the news page (team formed Aug 2024; 15 Sep 2026 seminar; 11 Sep Register story; Navigation Fund grant 8 Jul 2026; BlueDot rapid grant Jul 2026; leaderboard Feb 2026); SFF recommendations ($20k + $63k matching in SFF-2025, $457k in SFF-2026, via Players Philanthropy Fund, all correct). notes.khyentse-foundation: Confirmed: founded 2001 by Dzongsar Khyentse Rinpoche, mostly volunteer-run, no central HQ. Lynn Hoberg succeeded Cangioli Che as ED in 2024. The 2025 annual report PDF gives FY2025 total assets of US$52.6M and programme expenses of US$7.2M, frames 2025 around AI, and includes the ED's line on 'what Buddhism can offer AI'. The grants page confirms that five programmes (Buddhist Studies, PhD, Ashoka, Trisong, Individual Practice) have been paused since March 2026, explicitly citing the age of AI. Academic Development Grants are still open, which fits 'most' paused. Newsroom: 2 Sep 2026 and 24 Aug 2026 posts confirmed; Goodman Lecture #32 (Nehrdich, 'Buddhist Philology and AI', 12 Nov 2025) confirmed. Not verified: '50+ countries' and the Washington-state registration. Standpoint majority_world is a defensible judgement call (Bhutanese founder and chair) but borderline, since the foundation is US-registered with a globally distributed board. Sources: khyentsefoundation.org/who-we-are, /grants-and-scholarships, /newsroom, the 2025 annual report PDF, khyentsefoundation.org/team/lynn-hoberg.
notes.stanford-contemplation-by-design: The summit page and Stanford events listing confirm the 13th annual summit: 14-25 Oct 2026, free, mostly on Zoom with some in-person sessions, themed 'The Role of Contemplation in the Age of AI'. Its traditions span Buddhist, Islamic, Taoist, Christian, Quaker and secular. The about page confirms Tia Rich as founder and director at the Stanford Prevention Research Center, and both listed papers (2020 Frontiers, 2021 Prev Med Reports). A founding year of 2014, inferred from the 13th summit, is plausible. Ring potential (one AI summit) and transfer convening fit. Sources: med.stanford.edu/contemplation/summit.html, /about.html, events.stanford.edu CbD 2026 intro event.
notes.search-inside-yourself-leadership-instit: The team page confirms Peter Weng and Lindsey Kugel both as Executive Director (the caveat already notes this), Caro Hart as board chair, and co-founders Chade-Meng Tan, Marc Lesser and Philippe Goldin. The Humanitix listing confirms 'Addressing AI Anxiety', hosted by SIYLI with Google Principal Engineer Adam Bender and Weng: online plus limited seating in Santa Cruz, 13 Nov 1-3am CEST, which is 12 Nov 4-6pm PST, as the profile says. Founded 2012. I did not re-check the ProPublica figures. Ring potential (single workshop) and transfer protecting are reasonable. Sources: siyli.org/about/our-team, events.humanitix.com/addressing-ai-anxiety.
notes.data-workers-inquiry: Confirmed: run jointly by DAIR, the Weizenbaum Institute and TU Berlin under Miceli, with Dinika, Salim Wagner and Kauffman on the organising team (Laurenz Sachenbacher is also listed). The homepage says 19 data workers in 9 countries, matching the summary. The team page now lists about 30 community researchers, including people from South Africa and Colombia, so the count is growing. The ILO policy report (Salim Wagner, Miceli, Kinyua, Dinika, Hanna) was written ahead of the June 2026 ILO vote. Tag fix: transfer should be protecting, not into_builders. The taxonomy's into_builders means people who build or fund AI 'as people … organising inside labs'. Protecting explicitly covers a tradition defending the workers it serves, and DWI's subjects are outsourced annotators and moderators at Sama, Telus, Remotasks and others, not lab staff. Sources: data-workers.org, /about/team/, /policy-iloconvention/.
notes.fairwork: fair.work confirms Fairwork Certification is a non-profit company limited by guarantee spun out of OII and WZB, with Graham (ED), Feuerstein (CFO/director, WZB), Heeks (director) and Srinivasan (member). The OII reports page confirms Sama 2023 (GPAI), Sama and Appen 2025, the Cloudwork Report 2025, Tinkogroup 2026 and Germany Ratings 2026. notes.children-and-screens: About page confirms 2013, New York address and 'free from technology industry funding'. The grants page confirms the nearly $150k 2025 grant (Minnesota, Harvard, Stanford; 100 adolescents aged 13-17; 21 days). notes.the-rithm-project: The team page confirms Culver (Founder), Alison Lee (Chief R&D Officer), Miho Kubagawa (Head of Strategic Initiatives) and Sarah Selim (Somatics & Program Design). The team page confirms Robert Carter as Acting ED and Jennifer Newson as Lead Scientist, Cognitive and Mental Health. notes.integral-altruism: Checked integralaltruism.substack.com: 'The first year of integral altruism' (Euan McLean, 2 Mar 2026) confirms origin in a London EA meditation group 2023-25, reading group early 2025, summits Kent July 2025 and Cotswolds Dec 2025, six core stewards, London hub with Berlin/Paris, unfunded and seeking funding for McLean full-time. notes.rethink-wellbeing: Confirmed on rethinkwellbeing.org: Stichting Rethink Wellbeing (KvK 89206126), fiscal sponsor Players Philanthropy Fund, address Wapenveld NL; 285 participants, 35 countries, 66 facilitators, 97 funded places in 2025. notes.center-for-reducing-suffering: Checked the homepage and team page. The latest posts are 2 Oct 2026 ('Making Concern for Suffering Common Knowledge') and 17 Sep 2026, so status active is right.
